title: Typed Runlets Compiler and Safety Inference for Interactive Admin Tools
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Build a small, type-aware compiler that converts human-authored runlet scripts (interactive admin snippets) into typed, auditable task artifacts with static input validation and an optional safety-inference pass. This enables safer dry-run execution, better developer ergonomics in the admin CLI, and deterministic audit trails for support automation.

Why now: Support automation is expanding across Dedicated and Private customers; we need stronger guardrails around admin actions (typed inputs, runtime checks, and safety inference) so oncall can run remediation snippets without introducing cascading failures or data loss.

Scope:
- Design a compact typed-runlet language (JSON/YAML front-end) with primitives for idempotent operations, transactional boundaries, and annotated side-effects.
- Implement a compiler that emits a typed task schema + runtime manifest used by the admin CLI and runbook executor.
- Add a safety-inference pass that flags risky operations (destructive mutates, long-running jobs) and suggests guard conditions or confirmation levels.
- Integrate dry-run mode backed by the sandbox infra used by the ops lab; ensure no destructive side-effects while exercising telemetry paths.
- Expose structured telemetry: per-runlet latency, dry-run vs live success rates, and post-execution audit trace id.

Non-goals: Full language runtime, replacing the runbook orchestrator, or designing a new policy engine. We aim for a focused compiler + safety signals that plugs into existing runbook task runner.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Type-system complexity: we chose a small structural type system (strings, ints, enums, lists, maps with required/optional markers) rather than a full dependent type system to keep authoring simple for SREs.
- Static vs runtime checks: static checks will cover input shape, required confirmations, and obvious destructive actions. Runtime safety checks (quota, cross-service rate limits) remain runtime policies surfaced as warnings.
- Safety-inference heuristics will be conservative: prefer false positives with user-facing rationale and a one-click escalation path for senior oncall.

Progress so far:
- UX spec and example runlets drafted in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Typed+Runlets+Spec
- Prototype compiler PoC (reads YAML -> emits JSON schema + manifest) implemented: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runlet-compiler/pull/92
- Early telemetry hooks added to runbook executor; dry-run stub wired to ops-sandbox infra (internal feature flag gated).

Open questions:
- How to represent multi-step transactional semantics in the manifest (compensation steps vs strict transaction)? PM and SRE team leaning toward explicit compensation steps in the manifest.
- Confirmation UX: single checkbox vs typed passphrase for high-risk actions. Design prefers typed passphrase for destructive ops.

Testing & rollout plan:
1) Unit tests for compiler + schema validation (done: 85% coverage for core primitives).
2) Dry-run only beta with internal SRE team for 1 week (feature flag).
3) Canary to small subset of production operators with telemetry and automated rollback on error regression.
4) Gradual expansion with training doc and runlet authoring workshop.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in post-remediation rollbacks by 30% in first quarter after rollout.
- 95% of runlet executions include schema validation results in audit logs.
- No severe incidents attributed to runlet automation during the canary window.

Integration & dependencies:
- Depends on runbook dry-run sandbox infra (ENG-314159) for safe execution.
- Needs admin CLI flag work and UX changes (coordinate with DES and PM).

Rollout notes:
- Initial release is opt-in per-organization via Console toggle (console-2026.03).
- Provide migration helper that can try-convert legacy runbook snippets to typed runlets in dry-run mode.

Security review required: true
Customer impact: low
Release: console-2026.03
